cl.s: The Pan York and Pan Crescent sailed together from Burgas on 27 December 1947 (CORRECTED from 26 December per the 22:50 follow-up; matches Edo's route), were boarded unopposed by the British on 31 December 1947 and reached Cyprus on 1 January 1948, with 15,000+ Romanian and Bulgarian Jewish ma'apilim. The ships stayed anchored off Bogaz for five months while people were moved ashore.
cl.note: W4d findings 1 + 22:50 correction. Four sources agree on the timeline.

cl.s: The Pan ships' ma'apilim were detained at Karaolos (summer camps 55, 60, 61, 62 and 63), about 2 km northwest of Famagusta's old city. Pan York carried 7,557 passengers, Pan Crescent 7,612 (first-hand and ship-list sources). Avi Livney's testimony: Pan York passengers went first to the Xylotimbou winter camps while others cut their way into the Karaolos camps.

cl.s: No Jewish school existed in Vicovu de Sus; Miriam almost certainly attended the commune's Romanian state primary school (HYPOTHESIS, medium). The 1852 'Trivial Schule' was Romanianized after 1918; the Laura quarter school existed from ~1900. She was one of a small Jewish minority (1930: 334 Jews of ~8,200). Her schooling ended with the October 1941 deportation at 15. The 1891 relief campaign for the Laura schoolchildren was subscribed by M., A., D. MAIDANEK, H. LAUFER, M. BESNER, GRUBER - family names on the school's donor list.

cl.s: The IGRA 'Resource Guide: Romania' (= JewishGen InfoFile by Marcel Glaskie, Ra'anana, 7.12.2017) says civil registers older than 100 years are held in the county archives and open, newer ones only to proven family members. If that rule holds, in 2026 EVERY Galati birth up to 1926 is open to an ordinary request - Anna-Rose (1907), Philip (1912), Sali and Klara (born between 1915 and 1923?) and Yehuda (1924) - and the margins of the birth acts record later marriages (Eva's margin gives the 1941 marriage to Valeanu). Fani's act (D06, act 270/1909) shows no margin note on the image in the file; Eva's does. The guide has nothing on Galati, on post-1945 emigrants or on landsmanshaftn.
cl.note: Medium: the rule comes from a tool summary of a short guide and the 'up to 1926' reading is mine. The practical step is the archive request in lead L67.

cl.s: Galati landsmanshaft trail, checked: the only Galati society found is the 'Galatzer Handwerker KUV Society' at Mount Hebron Cemetery (Queens, New York), 'established in New York by immigrants from Galati'; the Mount Hebron page names no members, plots or years. The AJHS landsmanshaft catalog has no society with Galati in its name (Romanian societies are filed as 'United Rumanian Jews of America'); the Center for Jewish History Romania guide names YIVO landsmanshaftn from Bacau, Birlad, Botosani, Bucharest, Burdujeni, Radauti, Satu Mare, Bereg, Bukovina and Maramures, not Galati. Nothing found for Montreal, Toronto, Chicago or Tel Aviv. HYPOTHESIS (low): Peretz was a carpenter, so a craftsmen's society is the plausible one for a sibling who went to New York; no evidence that any sibling did.
cl.note: Low yield: Mount Hebron burial search (if public) for the society's section, then JOWBR for Rosenblum / Volman burials in that section.

cl.s: The post-1944 Galati archive holds named Jewish lists that fit the siblings question - USHMM RG-25.030M (63 reels, 51,350 images, 1940-1953): (a) Comitetul Democratic Evreiesc Galati (Fond 870, Inv. 957, reels 27-35), file 19, 1950-1952, 183 pp., 'Tabele nominale cu evidenta pe regiune a celor care au solicitat sa plece in Israel'; (b) same fond, file 34, 1951-1952, 199 pp., members' tables, references and autobiographies; (c) Comunitatea evreilor din Galati (Fond 643, reel 38), file 5, 1946, 'Tabele nominale cu evreii care au primit ajutoare la Comunitatea Evreilor din Galati'; (d) Prefectura Covurlui files 14/1945 and 21/1945 (repatriates from the USSR). If a sibling stayed in Galati until the 1950-52 Israel wave, file 19 is where the name and address would be; the 1946 aid list also shows who was in Galati and poor in 1946. The images are not online (Museum reading room or on-campus stations only). Whether any sibling is in them is unknown.
cl.note: High that the files exist; unchecked what they contain. Not a browser job: email the USHMM reference desk (look-up or copies for Rosenblum / Volman / Finkelstein) and SJAN Galati, which holds the originals (Fond 870 and Fond 643). Lead L63.

cl.s: The birth certificate records Yehuda's mother as ROSEMBLUM LEIA (Leia = Lea), with her husband's surname and no maiden name, and his father as ROSEMBLUM PERITZ (the Romanian spelling of Peretz). So Liza (Lea) Finkelstein is Leia in the civil register of 1925; Liza is the everyday form (as in the 1914 birth act of Eva). The family spelled the surname Rosemblum (with M before B) in Romanian papers.
cl.note: Search variants to add: Rosemblum, Peritz, Leia, Ionel. Strengthens the identification of the family tree (Perez and Lea) with the Galati couple Peritz and Liza of the 1906-1914 acts.

cl.s: CLOSED: 'Lea' and 'Liza' are the same woman - Yehuda's mother, Peretz's wife, daughter of Binyamin + Rifka Finkelstein. 'Lea' (לאה) was her Jewish name, used by the family (the family tree lists 'Lea (Liza) Finkelshtein', Lea FIRST; the self-declared Atzmaut manifest says 'Lea'); 'Liza' (diminutive of Elisabeta) was her Romanian civil name (act 46/1906, children's birth acts); 'Luisa' is a clerk's rendering on one Yad Vashem record. No second wife exists - every record naming Peretz's wife names this same woman.

cl.s: Emil (Mendel) Maidanek started as a tavern keeper in Vicovu-de-Sus (1923-24, Socec: 'Maidanek Mendel' among the Carciumari, listed right after his father-in-law 'Kurzberg Maier') and was a general merchant ('Kaufmann') by 1928 (Czernowitz assizes juror list). He was a recognized, established community member (assize-court juror 1928; separate charitable donor 1930). He appears in NO specialized merchant category (not among the ~20 grocers, not under timber, not among cattle merchants) - 'Kaufmann' as general merchant. Shop address and specific goods unknown.
cl.note: Q021. The 1925 Socec volume's Vicovu entry does NOT list Maidanek Mendel at all (Q124/S119). Family trade map: Abraham (tavern, Horodnic), Meir Kurzberg (tavern, Vicovu), Emil (tavern -> merchant), Chaim (wood, Seletin), Joel (cattle), Arie Priling (sawmill clerk).

cl.s: Who were Adolf and Josef to Emil? STILL OPEN. None of about 110 pages with 'Maidanek' (DiFMOE 1919-1941, Die Stimme 1956-2000, Hauster) names the father, wife or children of Adolf or Josef, or says what they were to Emil or to his father Abraham; no search found 'Joseph', 'Moses', 'Marie', 'Adolf und Josef', 'A. & J. Maidanek' or 'Maidanek & Co'. What the sources DO show: Adolf and Josef were the sawmill firm; Emil was a separate merchant in the same village.
cl.note: Age arithmetic (not evidence): Emil was born in 1898 and his father Abraham in 1871, whereas Adolf was about 48 in April 1934 (b. c.1886) and the candidate Josef was born in 1887 - so neither can be Emil's BROTHER (the inbox note F16 says 'Emil's brother is possible'; on the KB's dates (Abraham b.1871 would have been 15) it is not, unless Abraham's year is wrong). They could be his uncles (sons of Hersch, like Moses b.1886) or more distant cousins (e.g. sons of Moses & Marie). Deciders: Adolf's 1934 death record (L42), the firm file at SJAN Suceava and the CNR file at ANIC (L28), Josef's and Fany's later fate (L50).

cl.s: Dad's question, answered so far: Emil (Mendel) Maidanek did NOT own the Vicovu de Sus sawmill. The gazette names the firm's owners as Adolf and Iosif (1941) and Iosif alone (1943); in the press Emil is a separate merchant ('Maidanek Emil, Kaufmann, Oberwikow', 1928) and his own donation ('Emil Maidanek 65') is listed apart from 'Brueder Maidanek' (1930). He was also deported and died in Transnistria on 20.12.1941 (s5.emil_pot), i.e. before the July 1942 guard list and the 1943 lease (the expropriation itself may date from late 1940-41, s3.mo1942_details). Whether Adolf and Josef were his relatives at all is NOT settled (s8.kinship_still_open).
cl.note: An inference from absence: Emil's name is in none of the gazette entries and the press lists him apart from the firm. A silent partner cannot be excluded from lists that print only registered names; the trade-register file (L28) would close it. Supersedes the open reading in L23 ('answer so far: NO').

cl.s: GEDCOM forensics (R5, from rosenblum-geni_2026-10-07.ged): Ruhalia, Duvid, Resia and Shiloma sit in DAD'S OWN tree (Tree A, OYYV6NDADADE7HMLD7UPNT2J7B323CQ) in one contiguous ID block (2003990-2003993), each added via Smart Match confirmation ('אדם התווסף באמצעות אישור Smart Match'). Attestation differs per child: Ruhalia - TWO trees (Dad's + external Maidanek Tree B); Duvid - external Tree B + Dad's original family @F3; Resia and Shiloma - the family tree ONLY (zero citations from the otherwise-thorough external tree). Shiloma is marked M (male) - 'Shiloma' = Shlomo, a boy. Separately: the Radautz birth index (12,129 records, 1857-1929) contains ZERO Ruhalia/Shiloma and no 1920s Resia with Maidanek parentage - but with the caveat that NONE of Emil x Rosa's confirmed children (Josef 1923, Donzia 1924, Miza 1926, all Vicovu de Sus) are in the index either, so the index cannot test this family at all. The DiFMOE press corpus (1918-1940) has zero evidence any of the three names existed in Bukovina.
cl.note: Q212/Q049-supp2/Q049-supp. The batch hypothesis weakens for Resia/Shiloma (single-source); the decisive routes remain Dad and the ...23CQ tree owner (Q239, needs Bar).

cl.s: Taube Maidanek (née Haber) died 26-Apr-1888 aged 59 (death index entry 2635, P1140729) - born ~1829. This CONFIRMS the R1 Q438 chronology hypothesis: Taube Haber (b.~1829) was Joel Maidanek's wife (Joel d.23.3.1899 aged 70, b.~1829; the couple's only indexed child is Hersch b.Nov-1851, mother 'Haber Taube'). The couple's marriage predates the indexed registers (~1850 or earlier; no marriage in 1870-1929).
cl.note: Q533 (R4). The death act P1140729 may name Taube's parents (the Haber line); Joel's death act P1140874 should name his parents (standing pull list).

cl.s: Taube Haber appears in exactly one index row: as Hersch Maidanek's mother ('1427 | -Nov-1851 | Maidanek | Hersch | Maidanek | Joel | Haber | Taube | IMG_5888'). No birth, no marriage, no death for her in the indexes - born ~1820s-1830s, beyond the local indexes. The 20 Haber/Habermann marriages in the index (1877-1926) are a later generation. NOTE: the 'Taube Haber' of the 29.7.1931 Allgemeine ('Das Ehepaar Lazar Rudich und Taube Haber gehörte zu den ärmsten Bewohnern des neuen Dorfes' - murdered in Rupta) is a DIFFERENT woman. The 1947 summons is in Part II ('Partea a 2-a'), so any later court notice is in Part II too - Part III in these years is not where court notices sit. Only 1947-11-20 nr.269 and 1947-12-09 nr.285 post-date the summons and are court-notice issues, so they are the first two to open. If no judgment was published, it sits in the court file (Ilfov Tribunal Dos. 92/1947 - the SMBAN email draft).

cl.s: Anna's marriage window is refined by two weighted hypotheses. A (likelier): Anna is the SECOND wife - the 1929 wife was a first, unnamed wife; Anna married Osias 1930-1937 (the Jan 1930 'Frl. Anna Maidanek' birthday greeting is then accurate). B (weaker): Anna is the FIRST/ONLY wife, married before July 1929 (then the 1930 'Frl.' is loose usage by an admirer). Decisive: the Czernowitz marriage register or the 1929 wife's identity.
cl.note: Q211. If A, the KB's '1930-41' window narrows to 1930-37; if B, the wedding was <= mid-1929.

cl.s: Sali/Volman hunt: still open. (a) Husband's first name: only documentary lead is 'Hertz Volman (b.1910, Aug 1963, with family)' on an immigrant list (r5 Q041) - HYPOTHESIS A (untested): Hertz = Sali's husband. (b) 'Sima Volman (b.1910 Romania, ISA גל-15503-8 p67 row .21)' (r5 Q040): hypotheses = Sali herself (weak-against: a 1910 Galati birth act should exist online and Edo found none), Volman's sister, or another relative. (d) Decisive route: MyHeritage Jan 2023 release (1.7M ISA immigrant records, English-searchable, login needed - via Bar/Edo) or ISA Pinpoint גל-15503-8 (Bar's go-ahead).

n_adolf.notes: Timber industrialist of Unter-Wikow, died April 1934 aged 48 (D08). Place in tree unknown. 1920s-30s press (DiFMOE): Adolf Maidanek of Oberwikow - Radautz Jewish community councillor (1927), board member of the Bukovina Timber Syndicate (1928), district health fund (1932); the firm appears as Brueder Maidanek (1924, 1930). Round 2 (7.10 evening): full obituary in Czernowitzer Morgenblatt 26.4.1934 p.3 (signed Dr. L. Sch.): died of an insidious illness aged 48, charitable, popular with the peasants of Oberwikow; no relatives named. Juror list 20.4.1934: Adolf Maidanek, Maneutzi (Manauti). Parents still unknown (L42, X36). Stage 8 (B1 sprint): the firm Brueder Maidanek = Adolf si Iosif Maidanek (MO 28.1.1941 no.168); the factory is Iosif's alone by 1943 (MO 22.2.1943). All page images captured (N01, N02, N10, N14, N15). Kinship to Emil still open (age arithmetic: not his brother, L40). cl.s: One chain of records for the Vicovu de Sus sawmill, 1924-1943: 'Brueder / Gebrueder Maidanek' of Ober-Wikow, 2nd-largest sawmill at Vicov de sus with 15.1 wagons a month (Czernowitzer Morgenblatt 15.7.1924; donor lists 1924 and 1930) -> 'Maidanek A. & I.' (1929 list) -> 'Adolf si Iosif Maidanek, Vicovul-de-Sus' (export-licence list, MO 28.1.1941, no.168) -> 'fabr. Maidanek' expropriated and guarded by two state-paid guards (MO 6.7.1942) -> 'fabrica de cherestea, fosta Iosif Maidanek' leased out by the CNR (MO 22.2.1943). The owners named by the gazette are ADOLF (died April 1934) and IOSIF (Josef); the firm kept both names after 1934, and by 1943 the factory is Iosif's alone.
cl.note: 'Partly' because the link between the German press's 'Brueder Maidanek' and the gazette's 'Adolf si Iosif' rests on place, names and an unbroken run of dates (same village, same two first names, 1924-1943), not on a record that says 'brothers' - the gazette gives only the firm name. Strong inference, not stated in any single record. A second inference: Josef Maidanek was substitute INDUSTRY delegate beside the sawmill owner Josef Surkes (Straja sawmill, 1924 wagon list) on the Radauti tax-appeal commission 1936-37, so he was a timber industrialist (s6.josef_1937). Whether this Josef is n_josef_1887 stays a separate hypothesis (s4.sawmill_brothers).

cl.s: HYPOTHESIS (inference): 'Adolf' Maidanek of Oberwikow (d. April 1934) is Abraham Meidanek, b. 15.11.1884 Oberwikow, son of Moses and Marie - a secular name used for the Hebrew name Avraham. Evidence: (1) the Radautz births index (12,130 births of the Radautz, Solca and Vicov Jewish communities 1857-1929) contains NO child named Adolf in any Meidanek/Maidanek family, although Adolf was born c.1885-86; (2) the only boys of that age in the family are Abraham (15.11.1884) and Josef (12.5.1887), both sons of Moses and Marie of Oberwikow; (3) the firm's partners are 'A. & I.' (1929), 'Adolf si Iosif' (1941), 'Brueder' (1924), i.e. Adolf and Iosif were brothers working together, and Josef b.1887 fits Iosif; (4) Adolf for Avraham is attested (JewishGen's example 'Avraham hamechune Adolf'). Against: the 1934 obituary says aged 48, while Abraham was 49 years 5 months in April 1934 (a one-year slip is common in press notices); and it is not a standard pairing.
cl.note: Resolves the old worry 'Adolf is not Abraham' (X26, s3.adolf_not_abraham): that was about Emil's father Abraham b.1871 (d. Obodovka 1941), a different man. This is a third Abraham, b.1884. What would prove it: Adolf's 1934 civil death record (age, parents - L42), a birth or marriage record that gives both names, or a family document. Until then: probable, not proven.

cl.s: CORRECTION. The Hersch Maidanek who married Scheindel Ostfeld on 25.1.1881 (Radautz marriages index) is NOT Emil's grandfather. Emil's grandfather Hersch (Zvi, b. Nov 1851, son of Joel and Taube Haber, d. 19.1.1928) had his children with Jitte-Nesie Herer from Abraham (b.1871) to Mali (b.1893), and Jitte-Nesie lived until 1928, five years after the Scheindel of the 1881 marriage died (13.8.1923, aged 80, Vicovu de Sus). So the 1881 bridegroom is the other Hersch, son of Leizer and Sarah (Edo's claim hersch.5; stage 3 note on the 'two Hersch' deaths of January 1928). Consequence: the earlier remark that Moses Meidanek married Marie 'twelve days before Hersch, Emil's grandfather' (STATUS 7-8 Oct, s9.moses_kin_unproven) was wrong and is withdrawn; the date coincidence is no hint of kinship.
cl.note: Found by the WRITER while refreshing the deliverables (8.10 08:00). Inference rather than a record: it rests on Jitte-Nesie Herer being Emil's grandmother and Hersch's only wife in the records (cl.jite_alive_1901, s4.hersch_birth) - the 1881 marriage act would settle it by naming the bridegroom's parents (Leizer and Sarah vs Joel and Taube). What remains of the kinship case for Moses: the same rare surname in the same village, the 1891 donor initials, and the name Abraham (see s9.moses_kin_unproven).

cl.s: A geographic hint for the Putna side, not a proof: Joel was born in Karlsberg (Gura Putnei, 'mouth of the Putna'), Leiser was the rabbi of Putna, and Leiser's son Moses (c.1857) and Joel's son Hersch (1851) were both born in Mardzina (Marginea). Joel (b. c.1829) and Leiser (children born 1855-57) are of the same generation, so Leiser is a brother, cousin or other close relative of Joel - or unrelated neighbours with the same rare surname.
cl.note: Needs a document: Leiser's own marriage act (18.10.1877, book 2 p.1 no.5) and the 1881 act of the other Hersch name his father; Leiser's father = Abraham-Yaakov would make Leiser Joel's brother (lead L87).

cl.s: TENSION to resolve: the marriage index lists Leiser x Sure Adelstein on 18.10.1877 (book 2 p.1 no.5), but the 1881 act names Sure as the mother of Sossie (b. c.1855) and Moses (b. c.1857), and Edo's tree names 'Sara' as Leiser's wife. A marriage entered in 1877 cannot be the first marriage of the parents of children born in 1855-57 - unless it is a late civil registration (as for David in 1876 and for Hersch's birth in 1875), or Sure was a second wife who is named as mother in 1881. Also open: whether Sure Adelstein and Edo's 'Sara' are one woman.
cl.note: The 1877 act (lead L87) should show age and previous marital status of both.

n_lazar_v.notes: Married Eva Rosenblum, Bucharest 19.2.1941, act 441 (margin of D19). Surname reading disputed. Stage 8 (W2): no record after the 21.1.1947 summons; first MO II issues to open for a judgment: 1947-11-20 nr.269 and 1947-12-09 nr.285 (L53). Stage 11: Jean Valeanu b.1904 and Alexandru Valeanu of Timisoara rejected (s11.jean_valeanu_rejected, s11.alexandru_valeanu_rejected); weak candidates kept as HYPOTHESIS leads - Isac Valeanu b.1894 Iasi (L68), Adrian Valeanu b.1923 (s11.adrian_valeanu_hypothesis). Stage 12: no Valeanu in the Canadian Jewish press full text (s12.ia_valeanu_negative). Stage 14 (Ancestry A1): Lazar Vâleanu b.1912 in the Jewish Census 1942 (record 19001) and a Rio de Janeiro card pair Lazar / Eva Valeanu - possible, unread (L84, L85).

cl.s: Checked and rejected: the four JDC Names Index records that lead L47 listed as possible cards of Eva or Lazar Valeanu - 86990, 126345, 114127 and 133876 - are four unrelated Jewish DP cards: 86990 Elik Feldmann, b. 8/3/1909 Bucharest (Munich to France); 126345 Juda Perl, b. 5/20/1924 Viseu de Sus (Feldafing to the United States / Brazil); 114127 Stefan Lazar, b. 5/16/1921 Szombathely (Vienna to Australia); 133876 a girl born 11/3/1932 in Chernivtsi (Bucharest transient to Italy; name withheld, possibly living). Dates are as the database prints them (month/day/year, e.g. 5/20/1924). None is from Galati and none is a Rosenblum, Volman, Valeanu or Finkelstein. Card 114127 has the surname Lazar, which is Eva's husband's first name - a coincidence.
cl.note: Closes the four open ids of lead L47. Recorded so nobody opens them again.

cl.s: ANSWER TO LEAD L58. The Radautz marriage register, vol. II, p.32, entry 26 (January 1881; the day in the printed list is 13.1.1881), names the bridegroom as Moses Meidanek, 24, single, born in Mardzina (Marginea), a businessman (Geschaeftsmann) in Oberwikow house 1271, son of Leiser and Sure Meidanek of Putna. He is therefore the 'Moses, son of Leiser' of Edo's tree: n_moses_lm and n_moses_marie are one man, and the rabbi Leiser of Putna (per his daughter Silka's tombstone) is the father of the sawmill brothers' father. Moses's wife is Marie (entry 26 bride), his sister Sossie is entry 27.
cl.note: Cursive from a phone photograph, read by the orchestrator at 3000-4500 px; names are clear, the place word 'Mardzina' is the register's spelling of Marginea (the same village is written in Hersch's birth entry, s15.hersch_birth_act_1875). OPEN: the marriage index lists 'Leiser x Sure Adelstein, 18.10.1877' (book 2 p.1 no.5) - a marriage entered 20 years after Moses was born; either a late civil registration of an older marriage, or Sure is a second wife whom the clerk named as mother. The 1877 act names Leiser's own parents: lead L87.

cl.s: Are Moses and Marie Meidanek (parents of Adolf = Abraham and Josef) related to Emil's line? STILL UNPROVEN; the hints are only: the same rare surname in the same village (Oberwikow); Moses married Marie (also a Meidanek) on 13.1.1881, and in the next entry (no.27) Moses's own sister Sossie (daughter of Leiser and Sure, not Marie's sister) married Chaim Locker (CORRECTION, stage 14: an earlier version also counted the twelve days before the marriage of Hersch Maidanek and Scheindel Ostfeld, 25.1.1881, as a hint; that Hersch is another man, the son of Leizer - see s14.hersch_1881_other_man - so the coincidence is void); the Vicov donor list of 1891 shows M., A. and D. MAIDANEK (Dragusanul); a son named Abraham in 1884 could honour the dead Abraham-Yaakov (d.1860, Hersch's grandfather) - weak. HYPOTHESIS: Moses is a brother or first cousin of Hersch (b.1851, son of Joel and Taube). If a brother: Adolf and Josef are first cousins of Emil's father Abraham (b.1871) and first cousins once removed of Emil. No record says so.
cl.note: What would settle it: Moses's own birth or death record (he was born before the index starts in 1857, so look for his marriage act of 1881, which names his parents; Edgar Hauster can photograph it - see the 'Request Record' link), Adolf's 1934 death act, or any family document. Practical: ask Dad whether anyone ever said 'we had cousins with the sawmill'; and ask SJAN Suceava / Edgar Hauster for the 1881 marriage act of Moses x Marie (book P1120788) - it should give both fathers.

cl.s: The 1891 Laura (Vicovu de Sus) school-relief donor list (30 subscribers, Dragusanul) is fully extracted - the source gives INITIALS only. Three family donors matched to the tree: M. MAIDANEK -> Moses Maidanek (son of Leiser), HIGH (the only M-initial Maidanek businessman resident in Oberwikow; marriage act 13.1.1881: 'businessman in Oberwikow 1271'); A. MAIDANEK -> Abraham Maidanek (b.~1871, son of Hersch), MEDIUM (only adult Abraham in 1891, ~20; the Schankwirt of Oberhorodnik); D. MAIDANEK -> David Maidanek (b.c.1826, son of Abraham-Yaakov), MEDIUM-HIGH (only adult David in 1891, ~65). H. LAUFER, M. BESNER, S. HERER remain unmatched (not in the Radautz birth index as adults - Q226-FU).
cl.note: Q226/Q226-FU. Proves the Maidanek/Laufer/Besner/Herer families were established in Vicovu de Sus a generation before Miriam.

cl.s: Marie Maidanek, the bride of entry 26 (23, single), was born in Komanesti (a village; reading of the first letters tentative) and is the daughter of David and Dwora Maidanek of Radautz. The same parentage is written in the births of her sons Abraham (15.11.1884, book 4 p.30 no.165: 'Marie Maidanek, Tochter des David u. der Dwora Maidanek aus Radautz') and Josef (12.5.1887, book 4 p.114 no.70). David Maidanek of Radautz stands as godfather (sandek) at both births, and an 'Alter Maidanek of Radautz' at Josef's - probably Marie's brother Chaim-Alter. Marie's maiden name was Maidanek too: she married a man of the same surname.
cl.note: The mother is called 'Dwora' in all three acts; the 1876 index writes 'Devora Rosenberg' for David's bride, so Dwora's maiden name is Rosenberg if this is the same David (s15.marie_father_is_david_1876).

cl.s: Marie's father David Maidanek of Radautz is, very probably, the David Maidanek (born c.1826, died 1900 in Unterwikow, a widower) who married Devora Rosenberg on 6.6.1876 in Radautz (house 609) and whom the 1876 marriage index calls the son of Abraham and Mindel Maidanek (parents from Zaleszczyk, Galicia). For: the same two first names (David and Dwora / Devora) in the same town (Radautz), the same rare surname, fitting ages (David b.c.1826, Devora 48 in 1876 so b.c.1828, Marie b.c.1858), and David acts as godfather in 1884 and 1887. Against or open: the civil marriage of 1876 came 18 years after Marie's birth, so it is probably a late legalisation of a religious marriage (in 1875 Hersch's birth was also entered late on an order), or a second marriage with Dwora named as stepmother; the act of 6.6.1876 (images IMG_5417 / IMG_5423 / IMG_5426, vol. 1 p.28 no.78) will say.
cl.note: Next: read the 1876 act (P9, first priority) - it names David's parents and Devora's, and Marie's name may appear.

cl.s: ANSWER (probable, not proven) TO BAR'S QUESTION 'WERE ADOLF AND JOSEF OUR RELATIVES?'. Adolf (= Abraham b.1884) and Josef (b.1887), the sawmill brothers, are the sons of Moses and Marie. Marie was the daughter of David Maidanek of Radautz; David was the son of Abraham and Mindel Maidanek (1876 index), and Emil's great-grandfather Joel is 'ben Avraham-Yaakov' on his grave record, Mindel being documented only as David's mother. If David and Joel are brothers (sons of the Abraham-Yaakov who died in Radautz in 1860), then Marie is a first cousin of Hersch (Emil's grandfather), and Adolf and Josef are second cousins of Emil's father Abraham (b.1871) and second cousins once removed of Emil (Mendel). The kinship runs through their MOTHER; on the father's side Moses is a son of Leiser of Putna and no link to Joel is shown (Leiser's father is unknown). The sawmill itself is not Emil's (s8.sawmill_not_emil): it belonged to his probable second cousins.
cl.note: Weak points: (1) David is only presumed to be the husband of Devora (1876); (2) the Abraham of David's father and the Abraham-Yaakov of Joel's grave are presumed the same man (same generation, same town, same surname, but no document links them); (3) Joel's own parents are not named in any record seen. What would close it: the 1876 act (David's parents), Joel's marriage or a birth of one of his children with grandparents, a cemetery record of David, and the 1877 act of Leiser (the Putna side). Practical for Dad: 'very probably yes, as cousins through Marie'.

cl.s: Monitorul Oficial, Partea a II-a, nr. 44, 22.2.1943, p.1017 (Centrul National de Romanizare, public tenders): the CNR announces a sealed-bid auction for 10.3.1943, 10 a.m., at its auctions service (str. Mantuleasa 42, Bucharest) for a 2-year lease of 'fabrica de cherestea, fosta Iosif Maidanek' (the sawmill, formerly Iosif Maidanek's) in the commune of Vicovul-de-Sus, Radauti county, from an annual rent of 365,000 lei; bidders must be of Romanian ethnic origin and deposit 10 percent of the two years' rent. This is Josef's name on the factory: after Adolf's death (April 1934) the sawmill is attributed to Iosif alone.
cl.note: Fourth official-gazette mention of the factory (after MO 1941 no.168, MO 1942 nos.198-199, and the 1929 list). The text layer reads 'Mdidanek'; the image (N16) reads Maidanek. 'fosta' = former: by Feb 1943 the factory had been taken from its Jewish owner and was being leased out by the state. It does not say which Iosif (n_josef_1887 is the standing candidate, s4.sawmill_brothers) nor whether other co-owners existed. Result of the 10.3.1943 auction not found. Decider: the CNR file at ANIC (L28).

cl.s: Radauti County Prefecture name table 'Tabel Nominal de evrei cari s-au stabilit in orasul Radauti dela 6 Septembrie 1940 pana in prezent' (Jews who settled in the town of Radauti from 6.9.1940 to date; 398 numbered names; Hauster, Documents ch. 5): 'Maidanek Josef' is no.197 and 'Maidanek Fany' no.198. The sheet is undated; the book places it with the Siret police table of 15-17.5.1941, so spring 1941 (medium). The list gives no previous residence.
cl.note: Settles the 'which list and town' point left open in s6.josef_fany_1941. 'High' that both names are on the list; the date is medium. HYPOTHESIS (not proven): Josef moved from Vicovul de Sus to Radauti town after September 1940, when the factory was being taken over (guards appointed Nov 1940 - Mar 1942, s3.mo1942_details); the same list carries other Oberwikow / Putna names (Heitner, Herer, Dolberg, Rudich, ten Kurzberg entries). The list does not show where people came from, so this is a reading, not a record. Whether this Josef is n_josef_1887 is the standing hypothesis. Fate: L50.

cl.s: HYPOTHESIS (low): Sala Rozenblat, female, b. 4/12/15 as typed on the card (read as 4 December 1915; read month/day it would be 12 April 1915, only about 3.5 months after Eva's birth, i.e. impossible) Bukarest (JDC Jewish DP card 133247, Munich office, file US 4352, opened 7.6.1950, domestic worker, DPC Landsberg, destination USA, travelling alone) could be Yehuda's sister Sali. For: the first name Sala is the Romanian form of Sali, and the birth year falls in the gap 1915-1923 left by the known children.

Sali may therefore have married a Bessarabian or Soviet man and lived in the USSR or Moldova after 1940, and Misha may be a Soviet-born cousin who reached Israel, the US or Germany in the 1970s-90s. No record. Stage 6 also suggests 'Sali' may be Anna-Rose's family name (Anna-Rose is not in the family tree). Dad's Geni export shows, below Sali (deceased), only Misha and his descendants, all without surnames; Fani has the married name VOLMAN, birthplace 'Galaz' and no spouse; Philip's wife appears only as 'Liza' with the married name Rosenblum (no maiden name); Eva and Klara have no spouse or children. cl.s: Correction for the Meir Oren name-change search (lead L56): official name changes after 1948 were published in Yalkut Hapirsumim (IGRA database 'Name Changes after 1948', 222,795 records), not in Reshumot; changes of 1921-1948 are in the Palestine Gazette (IGRA 'Name Changes 1921-1948', 27,469). If Meir Oren's change from Rosenblum was official and after 1948, it should be in the first database; Reshumot is the wrong gazette name for 1950s notices. The B2 search of the Israel State Archives catalogue did not find the notice either (that catalogue does not hold the gazettes).
cl.note: Medium (tool summary of the IGRA page). Needs the IGRA login (lead L64).

cl.s: Meir Oren (Rosenblum): nothing found on the open web. English and Hebrew queries (born Galati / Iasi, Hebraized name, daughters, name change Rosenblum to Oren) return only unrelated Meir Orens - a business executive (marketscreener) and a professor at an Israeli health-policy institute - and generic pages. Yad Vashem documents/7532091 and photos/9799100 came up for the query but WebFetch reads only the 'YV360' header, so they are UNREAD. HYPOTHESIS (an idea, not evidence): a Hebraization Rosenblum -> Oren would have been announced in the Israeli official gazette (Reshumot, name-change notices, c.1949-1960s), which gives the previous name and address and so could prove who he was.
cl.note: Whether he is Peretz's brother at all is doubtful - X38. Leads L56 (Reshumot, Geni, Dad) and L47 (the two unopened Yad Vashem ids).

cl.s: the family tree (s6.dad_rosenblum_sibs) makes Meir Oren (Rosenblum) Peretz's BROTHER, but Peretz's father was himself Meir Rosenblum, already dead on 1.7.1906 ('Meer Rosemblum defunct', D02) - and Peretz (b.1879) has a known brother Itzik (1908 marriage). Ashkenazi families name children after the dead, not the living, so a son Meir born while his father Meir was alive is unlikely (a posthumous son would be the exception). HYPOTHESIS, not evidence: Meir Oren is a NEPHEW or cousin of Peretz (e.g. a son of Itzik or of another brother, named for the grandfather), or the family tree is wrong.
cl.note: Reasoning from naming custom only; no record names Meir Oren's parents. The sibling link stays in the tree as 'partly / low' (not removed): asking Dad (L56) is the quickest test. Recorded as conflict X38.

n_carl_chaim.notes: Born 7.12.1889 Unter-Wikow (Vicovu de Jos); left Bukovina 1909; shoemaker and leather dealer in Hamburg-Harburg; German army WWI; wife Helene nee Rosenbaum; sons Herbert (1920, died Lodz ghetto 1942) and John (b.1924, sent to the USA in 1934, became a teacher). cl.s: 'Maidanek Fany', no.198 on the same Radauti list, directly after Josef (no.197). HYPOTHESIS: Josef's wife. The adjacency is weak evidence because the list is alphabetical (Maier follows at nos.199-200), so any Maidanek would stand there; a sister, daughter or sister-in-law is equally possible. Her maiden name and origin are unknown, and no other record naming 'Fany Maidanek' was found in DiFMOE (inbox F16).
cl.note: Entered as an unplaced person so that the record is findable; no relationship has been entered. Lead L50.

cl.s: Czernowitzer Morgenblatt 6.1.1931, p.4, 'Bunter Abend in Oberwikow' (held 20.12.1930 by the Jewish poor-relief association, Armen-Unterstuetzungsverein, in the hall of the 'Deutsches Haus'): thanks go to the committee - 'Frl. Bartfeld, Frau Bartfeld, Frau Ellenbogen, Frau Edelstein, Frau Helene Maidanek und Frau Theiler sowie die Herren Ellenbogen und Besner'. HYPOTHESIS: Helene is the wife of Adolf or Josef Maidanek (Emil's wife is Rosa); a widow or daughter-in-law is also possible.
cl.note: 'High' for the text, low for who she was. The inbox transcribed the last name as 'Theller'; the image (N13) reads Theiler. Not placed; lead L51. Brings the number of Oberwikow Maidanek households in the press (Adolf, Josef, Emil, plus Helene's) to at least three.

cl.s: Benisch Feldhammer x Scheindl Laufer: religious marriage ~1895; civil marriage 4-Dec-1901, Radautz (marriage index entry 1185, register P1120516; 'Feldhammer Berisch x Laufer Scheindl' - 'Berisch' is the clerk's rendering of Benisch). Children (Radautz birth index, all b.Oberwikow): Efroim (15-Dec-1896, Book 5 p.106 no.254, P1100737), Pesach Leib (15-Oct-1900, Book 5 p.378 no.188, P1100883), Seinwil (3-Jun-1906, Book 7 p.305 no.118, P1100327). Each birth entry cross-references the parents' marriage (vol. III p.121/122, entry 160, 04.12.1901, P1120526). Daughters Pepi and Rosa (Siret 1941 household, s18.siret_feldhammer_household). The bride Scheindl Laufer is Bar's Laufer line - a new Feldhammer-Laufer link.
cl.note: Q248-supp/Q255. Scheindl's parents: BLOCKED - not in the Radautz birth index (b.~1866-1876 est.); needs the P1120526 marriage image or Dad (s18 lead).

cit.q: 'Feldhammer Berisch x Laufer Scheindl', 4-Dec-1901; three births to 'Feldhammer Benisch' + 'Laufer Scheindl/Schendl'

cl.s: The Siret May-1941 table's four Feldhammers (83 Benisch, 84 Pepi, 85 Rosa, 86 Scheindel) map exactly onto Benisch x Scheindl's household: father Benisch, mother Scheindel, daughters Pepi and Rosa. NOT Abraham Feldhammer's household. The three sons (Efroim, Pesach Leib, Seinwil) are NOT in the Siret table; their fates unknown. The Siret Pepi is Benisch's daughter - NOT Miriam Feldhammer nee Maidanik's daughter Pepi.
cl.note: Q251. Answers Q248's question.

cl.s: A SECOND Feldhammer family: Salomon Feldhammer x Dewora Brane nee Uscher ('Brane' a middle name) - religious marriage 11-Nov-1900, civil certificate Storozynetz 12-Apr-1907 No.72 (Trauungsmatrik Storozynetz B.II fol.109 no.29; NOT in the Radautz marriage index). Children, both b.Galanestie/Galinesie (Storojinet district): Fabian (1-Apr-1907, Book 8 p.132 no.57, P1090923; legitimized per the 1907 certificate) and Karl Meier (4-Sep-1909, Book 9 p.68 no.139, P1090577; m.Klara Fröhlich - b.1909 Storojinet, daughter of Hersch and Rifka Fröhlich - on 24.11.1933 in Storojinet, per a later Romanian annotation). Salomon of Barna was an assize juror (Kimpolung, Oct 1930). Different towns and marriage districts from Benisch's family - kinship to Benisch or Abraham unproven (separate-branch HYPOTHESIS).

cl.s: Abraham Feldhammer (husband of Miriam the elder, m. Vicovu de Sus 1.3.1922) and Benisch Feldhammer were BOTH independent householders in Vicovu de Sus in October 1937 - named adjacently among the Jewish residents whose windowpanes were smashed (18.10.1937). Benisch was almost certainly Abraham's close relative (brother or father/son).

cl.s: Osias Ovadis, restaurateur in Czernowitz: opened a restaurant at Strada Vasile Voda (July 1929; violent dispute with landlord Jakob Raileanu - knife drawn, 10,000 lei missing from the till; both sides published rebuttal letters); the Ovadis family also ran the 'Delfabrik Ovadis' oil factory (Pruthgasse, burgled March 1929); 'Restaurateur Ovadis' scammed of 300,000 lei by a counterfeit-money 'Wunderwasser' gang (Dec 1936-Jan 1937, released after preliminary investigation); Restaurant Ovadis, Piata Ghica Voda 5, assaulted in a dine-and-dash (Feb 1938) and still advertising Nov 1939. Brother-in-law Josef Burg named as present at the 1929 brawl.
cl.note: Q193-supplement/Q210. The 1941-44 fate: the restaurant was almost certainly expropriated under decree-law 2507 (3.9.1941) - HYPOTHESIS on the specific property, legal mechanism certain.

cl.s: The 'Holzindustriefirma V. Axelrad' of Vicovul de Sus owned its own sawmill - a SECOND Vicov sawmill besides the Maidanek brothers'. In 1927 the firm was to transport 7,500 kg of Decouville narrow-gauge rails from Brodina to its sawmill; the shipment was confiscated en route as alleged Austro-Hungarian army war booty. The firm proved private purchase with its own funds, the criminal case was dropped, and the court heard its damages claim (concluded 6.2.1937). The 'V.' initial is unresolved - likely Hersch/Mechel Axelrad's firm (or an OCR artifact); the Maidaneks were ~7x larger (1924: Brüder Maidanek 15.1 wagons/month vs Hersch Axelrad 2 wagons/month).
cl.note: Q507 (R1+R2), Q515, Q524. The Jakobeny sawmill fire ('Ferma Goldenzweig, Scheuermann u. Axelrad') is a DIFFERENT Axelrad in a different town - not the Vicov firm.

n_anna_besner.notes: b.23.7.1891, father Mendel Besner, mother listed 'Chewed Korber' (P1110070) - anomaly: all siblings' mother is Sluwe Devora Habermann.

cl.s: ANOMALY: Anna Besner (b.23-Jul-1891, P1110070) has father Mendel Besner but mother listed as 'Chewed Korber' - while all her siblings' mother is Sluwe Devora Habermann. Hypothesis (weak-medium): Mendel was widowed ~1890 and remarried Chewed Korber, with Anna (b.Jul-1891) the first child of the second marriage. No death for Sluwe Devora and no second Mendel marriage in the indexes support it - the hypothesis rests only on the two birth entries' different mothers. Alternative: indexer misattribution on P1110070. The register image is decisive (standing pull list).
cl.note: Q543. 'Chewed' is a real given name in the index (Chewed Kupferberg x Salomon Korber; Chewed/Jochewed Korber x Jechiel Faust) - a plausible real person, not an obvious misreading.

n_karoline_horer.notes: x Salomon Weisler 6.9.1883 (P1120795 - the act says HÖRER). The 1891 birth entry spells her 'Herer' - likely clerk confusion. Parentage open (1883 act names her parents).

cl.s: Salomon Weisler (Schulem) married Karoline Horer on 6-Sep-1883 (marriage index #321, act P1120795). The 1883 marriage act says the maiden name is HÖRER; the daughters' birth entries spell it 'Herer' (1891) and 'Hörer' (1897). 'Herer' is a distinct large Radautz family (100+ birth entries 1854-1926, multiple branches: Efroim x Regina; Abraham x Malke Wagner; Pinkas x Hendel Hechtling; Michel x Mina), NOT spelling instability - and the families intermarried (Hörer Moses b.8-Feb-1881, father Hörer Itzig, mother Herer Frime). The 1891 'Herer' for Karoline is most likely a clerk's confusion between the two similar surnames; the marriage act (primary document) wins. The act images (P1120795, P1110066) would show the original handwriting. Karoline's own parentage is open - the 1883 act names her parents (the Seide-Karoline bridge, standing pull list).

cl.s: Seide Hörer was a prominent Radautz communal figure for 16+ years: 1919 brith-milah donor ('Seide Hörer a 5 K', OJZ 19.7.1919); ELECTED to the Radautz Jewish community council in July 1934 on Liste 3 (Allg 1.8.1934 - the first elections in 25 years, 1,566 of 1,948 voters); appointed to the Gerent's advisory board in March 1935 (Morgenblatt 11.3.1935); on the 1935 Kultusrat 4-list roster (Liste 1, Allg 16.5.1935). Yet he has NO birth or marriage in the Radautz/Solca/Vicov indexes (1857-1929) - born before 1857 or outside the indexed communities. He is very likely of Karoline Horer's (m.1883) generation - possibly a brother or cousin - but unproven.
cl.note: Q509. His obituary may be in Die Stimme (1980s-90s) - browser route.

cl.s: Leib Gerschon Wolfram (b.~1868) was a substantial Oberwikow grocer-merchant (Greisler): he owned a big house in the village center where he had run a grocery store for many years, flat attached. On 3-Nov-1932, around midnight, four masked rifle-armed bandits broke in, dragged the 64-year-old from bed, beat him terribly with rifle butts (severe injuries), stole 12,000 Lei from a hiding place plus 20,000 Lei of shop goods, and carted them off in a waiting wagon (the same gang suspected in a recent Falcău robbery). Follow-up 2.12.1932: additional loot - Austrian silver coins (5 fl., 2 K, 1 Kr.), Russian silver coins, a gold ladies' wristwatch. No trial or arrest coverage found (DiFMOE 0).
cl.note: Q506, Q516. Leib d. after Nov 1932. His birth (~1868) and parentage are not in the indexed births (pre-1857 coverage); the DAChO marriage act (~1886) would name his parents.

n_ester_dollberg.notes: Of Putna. d.mid-July 1938 (long illness). Mourned by two sons: an engineer (technical director of the Putna cement factory - given name unknown; Heinrich Dollberg b.1912 hypothesis) and a lawyer (Dr. M. Dollberg of Vatra-Dornei hypothesis). Not yet placed among the Dollberg lines.

cl.s: The Putna Dollbergs were a timber-merchant family active in KKL and community giving through the 1920s-30s: 'Brüder Dollberg' (Dollberg Brothers) timber firm - 1500 kg production, 26 kg stock, 4.5 wagons monthly (Morgenblatt 13.7.1924) + Saul Dollberg (670 kg stock, 2 wagons monthly, same stats; also a 3.7.1923 school-fund donor); KKL/donor lists 1924-1930 naming Wolf, Markus, Noe/Noa, Josef, Max, W. jun., Jakob, Saul, Feibl, Seide Besler, Isak, I., O., N., Rosa, Estera Dollberg (1924: 'Salzberger - Dollberg' KKL committee; 1925: Noe, Josef, Max, W. jun., Jakob; 1926: Rosa collector, Dina collector; 1930: W., N., O., I., Isak). Estera Dollberg of Putna died mid-July 1938 after long suffering ('Todesfall. Dieser Tage starb in Putna nach langem Leiden Frau Estera Dollberg.. Um Frau Dollberg trauern zwei Söhne, und zwar Ingenieur Dollberg, der technische Leiter der Zementfabrik an Putna und ein anderer Sohn, der Advokat ist.' - Morgenblatt 19.7.1938). Her husband is not named; her age is not given. The lawyer is likely 'Adv. Dr. M. Dollberg, Vatra-Dornei' (19 DiFMOE items 1923-1937 - the ONLY Dollberg lawyer in the region; given name never spelled out) - hypothesis medium; the engineer's given name is unknown (Heinrich Dollberg b.1912 hypothesis, medium).
cl.note: Q508, Q561, Q562, Q563, Q566, Q568. Sibling/cousin relationships among the Putna Dollbergs are not stated in any item.

cl.s: Isak Alper (b.~1904) was an authorized orthopedic specialist / prosthetist of Czernowitz: 'Prothesen | Kunstbeine, Geh- und Stützapparate, Lederkorsette.. beim autorisierten orthopädischen Spezialisten Isak Alper - Czernowitz, Str. Podgoriei 6 (Weinberggasse)' (Morgenblatt 12.9.1931); 'Orthopäde ISAK ALPER geeicht!, beeideter Sachverständiger, Cernăuți, strada Stefan cel Mare 8' (Morgenblatt 25.12.1934). The prosthesis ads ran as a near-daily series through March-April 1936, then stop. Address timeline: Podgoriei 6 (1931) -> Ștefan cel Mare 8 (from Dec 1934). In June 1937, six months after marrying Fani Rosenblum (15.12.1936), he was advertising himself for ANY work ('Bin fleißig, gebildet, verläßlich, repräsentabel und sprachenkundig.. erbitte jedwede Verdienstermöglichung', Allg 23.6.1937). He died in Haifa ~April 1969 aged 65: 'In Haifa: Im Alter von 65 Jahren verschied Isak Alper, Orthopädist, früher Czernowitz. Es trauern seine Gattin Fanny Alper und die Tochter Ruth, verehl. Feiler.' (Die Stimme 1.5.1969).
cl.note: Q366-followup (R4). Routes: Yad Vashem 'Isak Alper'/'Fanny Alper'/'Ruth Feiler' (browser, Bar logins); MyHeritage Israel graves (Isak d.1969 Haifa - gravestone gives exact birth date); the 1936 Czernowitz marriage act (DAChO - names Fani's parents, the last direct test of the Peretz-x-Liza link).

CAUTION: the address is now shown to be a multi-family tenement, not a family home - a third couple (Marcus Vogel x Sara Goldenberg) married at the same address in Nov 1938 ('Marcus Goldenberg, strada Ion Creangă 47, cu Sara Vogel', Allg 30.11.1938), which modestly WEAKENS the address argument; the sister hypothesis still stands on the name pairing. No post-1938 trace of Smil/Ghizela Birnbaum in the press (2 'Smil Birnbaum' hits total: the 1938 notice + an unrelated 1926 Czech photo-factory ad). Whether they are Peretz x Liza's daughters is NOT proven - the DAChO 1938 civil marriage act (names her parents) is decisive (archive-gated).

cl.s: Adjacent Czernowitz cluster, probably UNRELATED to the Galati Finkelsteins: 'Amalia Flintenstein' x Elias Fleischer (cab driver from Siret) 29.10.1936, Ion Creangă 3 (Tagespost); 'Julia Flintenstein' x Joses Echärs 21.11.1935 (Morgenblatt); 'Igo Flintenstein, 9 Jahre' d.28.5.1936, Ion Creangă 45 (Tagespost); a 1926 birthday greeting from 'Brüder Schächner'. The spelling 'Flintenstein' is verified via ALTO word-level OCR (not a misread of Finkelstein); pre-1900 German/Austrian hits show it is an attested independent surname. Zero Flintenstein in the Radautz birth/marriage indexes; zero 'Flintenstein' + Galati/Galatz press link. HYPOTHESIS (medium): a distinct Czernowitz family, not Bar's Galati Finkelsteins - pending the DAChO 1935/1936 marriage acts (parents' names) and Yad Vashem 'Flintenstein' + Czernowitz (browser). DiFMOE pids for the 1932/1926/1936 Flintenstein items are now dead - capture verbatim on first read.

n_moses_dolberg.notes: b.8.3.1882 Putna, son of Salomon Dollberg x Silka Maidanek/Meidanek. No marriage, no children, no death in the Radautz indexes; no press trace. The Dr. Moses Dollberg (Israel, Emunah fraternity) is a different man.

cl.s: Both sons of Salomon Dollberg x Silka Maidanek/Meidanek disappear from the Radautz registers. Moses Dolberg (b.8-Mar-1882 Putna, P1110181): no marriage, no children, no death in the indexes; no press trace. David Dollberg (b.~1886 Putna): #2387 Dolberg David x Lindermann Ester, 22-Aug-1920, P1120461 (the family's only forward trace); no children (1921-1929), no death, no press. The 'Dr. Moses Dollberg' (advokat, Ehrenpräsident at the Emunah fraternity's 120th-semester celebration in Israel, Die Stimme 1.8.1963) is a DIFFERENT man - do not conflate. The Silka Maidanek x Salomon Dollberg line (m.1877) has no documented grandchildren in the Radautz indexes.

n_salomon_dolberg.notes: x Silka Maidanek/Meidanek (m.1877); children Moses b.1882, David b.~1886 (both born Putna). The Maidanek-adjacent Dollberg line.

n_wolf_dolberg.notes: b.20.12.1892 Unterwikow, son of Jacob/Jankel Dollberg x Keile Einhorn. Hypothesis (medium-strong): the 1924 timber-stats Wolf Dollberg and KKL donor; 'Brüder Dollberg' may be his firm.

n_judith_niederhoffer.notes: b.30.4.1921, daughter of Jankel Niederhoffer x Ester Beile Axelrad.

n_josef_niederhoffer.notes: b.21.9.1924, son of Jankel Niederhoffer x Ester Beile Axelrad.

n_anna_niederhoffer_j.notes: b.2.4.1926, daughter of Jankel Niederhoffer x Ester Beile Axelrad (distinct from Anna Niederhoffer b.1901, Michel's daughter).

n_hillel_horer.notes: b.26.12.1913 (P1090321), son of Hersch Hörer x Sara Weitmann.

n_isak_horer.notes: b.28.2.1920 (P1080869), son of Hersch Hörer x Sara Weitmann.

n_israel_kastner.notes: b.16.8.1870, son of Meier Moses Kastner x Scheindel Ostfeld (the elder Scheindel).

n_esther_kastner.notes: b.5.11.1872, daughter of Meier Moses Kastner x Scheindel Ostfeld (the elder).

n_jacob_wolf_kastner.notes: b.25.6.1878, son of Meier Moses Kastner x Scheindel Ostfeld (the elder).

n_dawid_kastner.notes: b.20.9.1880, son of Meier Moses Kastner x Scheindel Ostfeld (the elder).

n_heni_pessi_maidanek.notes: b.17.6.1904, daughter of the 'other Mendel' Maidanek x Gitel Frime Winter.

n_mariasse_maidanek.notes: b.22.12.1905, daughter of the 'other Mendel' Maidanek x Gitel Frime Winter.

n_leib_maidanek2.notes: b.1.10.1907, son of the 'other Mendel' Maidanek x Gitel Frime Winter.

n_joel_maidanek2.notes: b.16.1.1909, son of the 'other Mendel' Maidanek x Gitel Frime Winter.

n_silka_dolberg.notes: née Maidanek/Meidanek; x Salomon Dolberg (m.1877); sons Moses b.1882, David b.~1886 (both Putna). The line has no documented grandchildren in the Radautz indexes.

n_ester_lindermann.notes: x David Dolberg 22.8.1920 (P1120461) - the family's only forward trace.

n_jakob_dolberg.notes: Jankel/Jakob Dollberg of Putna; x Keile/Kele Einhorn; children Hersch b.1887, Ettel b.1889, Schoel Salomon b.1890, Anna b.1897, Wolf b.1892 (Unterwikow).

n_nussen_katz.notes: x Ettel Katz née Dollberg ~1924 (outside the Radautz marriage index); son Leo b.8.4.1925.

n_markus_dolberg.notes: Markus Dollberg of Putna; x Dora/Dewora Kahan/Kahn (married Sereth); seven children 1892-1905, all born Putna.

n_josef_alter_kahan.notes: x Mina Dollberg 30.1.1910 (P1120200); surname matches the bride's mother's maiden name (possible kin marriage, unproven).

n_feibel_dolberg.notes: Feibel/Feiwel Dollberg; x Scheindel Kutmann/Gutmann; children Schoel Salmen 1893, Anna 1895, Emil 1899.

n_feibel_dolberg2.notes: Feibel Dollberg (second, distinct from the Scheindel-Kutmann husband); x Resi Tannenzapf; children Emma 1905, Robert 1906, Sarah 1910, Heinrich 1912.

n_david_jonas_faust.notes: b.6.11.1890 Solka, son of Jechiel Faust x Jochewed Korber. x Toni Ber 19.6.1924 (P1110970) - AMBIGUOUS: could be the other David Jonas Faust (b.11.1.1889, son of Efroim x Jetti Reicher).

n_efroim_faust.notes: x Jetti Reicher; son David Jonas b.11.1.1889 Solka (the other David Jonas Faust).

n_jetti_reicher.notes: x Efroim Faust; son David Jonas b.11.1.1889 Solka.

n_chaje_alper.notes: Berhometh Jewish community donor (1927: 150 Lei; 1934: 50 Lei to Misrachi). Convicted 27.2.1938 with Juda Ramler, Bernhard Scrumpn(?), A. Adler, Bernhard Kate of forging/distributing 20-Lei coins. No age/address in press. Kinship to Fani's Alper line unproven.

n_riwa_alper.notes: b.~1904 (34 in Feb 1938), of Str. Cogalniceanu 28. Arrested 26.2.1938 for harboring the 20-Lei counterfeiters and their equipment; NOT among the five convicted 27.2.1938. Kinship unproven.

n_ehaie_alper.notes: Landlady ('Frau Ehaie Alper') who hosted the 20-Lei counterfeiting workshop at Str. Kogalniceanu 28; arrested 26.2.1938 with Richard Katz and Adler, ~100 fake coins seized. Identity vs Chaje Alper open (X50).

n_aron_alper.notes: Vama merchant: Zionist donor 1925-1932; Vama commerce delegate on the 1937 district commission ('Vama: Handel: Aron Alper'). Daughter Dora x Dollinger (Bacău, str. Piața 16, ~1926).

n_dora_dollinger.notes: Daughter of Aron Alper of Vama; married a Dollinger, moved to Bacău (str. Piața 16) by Sept 1927 (her own paid announcement).

n_hermann_alper.notes: d.~Feb 1982; buried Har HaMenuchot, Jerusalem (Askara 6.2.1983); widow Klara Alper-Hofer. Arc: Czernowitz - Bucharest - Jerusalem. Identity with the Berhometh Hermann: weak hypothesis.

n_manfred_alper.notes: Arrested 29.10.1932 among Czernowitz communists (Organisation revolutionärer Mittelschüler); b.~1913 or later (all defendants under 19). No post-1932 trace. Kinship unproven.

n_salomon_alper.notes: Meat-hall (Fleischhalle) owner, Bräuhausgasse 44 (1931 break-in: meat, 2,000 Lei, 8,000-Lei fur stolen); at str. Podgoriei 6 in 1925 (lost-and-found: white sheep). Hypothesis (medium-strong): Isak Alper's father.

n_norbert_alper.notes: x Klara Alper; daughters Malka (1921-2011, Netanya) and Shani (Shoah victim with her family). Named on Malka's gravestone ('בת קלרה ונורברט ז״ל'). Press-invisible; town/dates/fate unknown.

n_klara_alper.notes: x Norbert Alper; mother of Malka and Shani. Press-invisible.

n_malka_alper.notes: b.1921 d.2011, buried Netanya Shikun Vatikim (sect.18, plot 4-46): 'מלכה אלפר' nickname 'מלציה', 'בת קלרה ונורברט ז״ל'. Gravestone memorializes her sister Shani and her family who perished in the Shoah.

n_shani_alper.notes: Sister of Malka Alper; married with children; perished in the Shoah with her family (Malka's gravestone). BLOCKED: needs Yad Vashem browser-gated, Dad, or DAChO (L179).

n_pepi_jurman.notes: d.1965 Netanya (obituary 1.10.1965: 'früher Czernowitz'); x Prof. Josef Jurman; daughters Hana Kelmer (m. Ing. Tobias Kelmer), Karla Haber (m. Magister Jeshaiahu Haber). Kinship to Norbert x Klara Alper unproven. Note: gravestone 'פפי בת אברהם מרדכי יורמן' is the married name.

n_josef_jurman_prof.notes: x Pepi née Alpern (d.1965 Netanya); father of Hana Kelmer and Karla Haber. One press trace (the obituary).

n_hana_kelmer.notes: Daughter of Josef x Pepi Jurman; m. Ing. Tobias Kelmer. LIVING POSSIBLE: name + relationship only.

n_karla_haber.notes: Daughter of Josef x Pepi Jurman; m. Magister Jeshaiahu Haber. LIVING POSSIBLE: name + relationship only.

n_malka_frisch.notes: x Chaim Frisch (butcher), 23.2.1938, both of Str. Romana 63. Her only press trace is the wedding notice.

n_chaim_frisch.notes: Butcher (Selcher), of Str. Romana 63; x Malka Alper 23.2.1938. Single trace.

n_josephine_alper.notes: Czernowitz donor: 600 Lei to the Jewish Tuberculosis Association on the yahrzeit of her father Chaim Besen (1937). Her Alper husband's first name garbled in the press; not identified.

n_oskar_alper.notes: Timber exporter; x a daughter of Chaim Besen (obituary 18.2.1935). Timber-industry figure 1936 (executive committee). Firm name, marriage date, children not in the press.

n_emanuel_alper.notes: One press trace: 50-Lei Berhometh donation (OJZ 25.4.1926). Not the 'I. Alper' of the 1926 Berhometh wedding notice.

n_gerta_alper.notes: Dance student; one press trace (20.2.1937 recital review). No family attribution.

n_bernhard_alper.notes: Footballer (Sportklub Borochow); one press trace (7.10.1937 thank-you to Dr. M. Klier).

n_s_alper_singer.notes: 'The youthful singer S. Alper' (22.1.1933, 15.12.1934 Zionist evenings). No full name anywhere.

n_max_alper.notes: One trace: 1939 tombstone notice. The M. Alper forwarding-agent hypothesis (1923-1933) unproven.

n_robert_weiner.notes: Str. Romana 63; two traces (1937 donor list; 19.11.1937 newspaper contest prize). No profession, no family.

n_chaim_besen.notes: b.~1863, d.18.2.1935 Czernowitz (aged 72, of Str. Miron Costin 16). Timber merchant 'for decades'. Obituary: one son owned the Holznägelfabrik, the other continued the wood business; two daughters - one x timber exporter Oskar Alper, the other x an Amtsrichter named Stauber (surname garbled). Whether 'Besen' = 'Besner' (paternal surname): open hypothesis, no positive evidence.

n_salomon_besen.notes: Timber merchant; house owner Maria Theresiengasse 14 (cut a tenant's rent 1931); Kultusbeirat Finanzsektion 1922; Fericirea dowry-society treasurer 1925; 1937 Handelskammer candidate; 1938 robbery one-liner. Press trace 1922-1938. Kinship to Chaim Besen unproven.

n_josef_bierer.notes: b.25.11.1870, d.late Nov 1937 Vienna (buried Wiener Zentralfriedhof 1.12.1937). Röntgenologist (Röntgeninstitut); CORRECTION: GIDEON's FATHER, not brother. Son of Dr. Ruben Bierer (Herzl's friend, Kadimah founder, Leibarzt to King Milan Obrenović). Herzl-circle Zionist founder, WWI hero, builder of the Czernowitz Jewish hospital's X-ray department.

n_gideon_bierer.notes: Orthopedic surgeon (ex-Lorenz Vienna clinic); Institut für orthopädische Chirurgie, str. Romană 21; exhibited at the 1935 Petermarkt (Anerkennungsdiplom). Son of Dr. Josef Bierer.

n_ruben_bierer.notes: Leibarzt to King Milan Obrenović (Belgrade), then Lemberg; with Nathan Birnbaum, Dr. Schmierer and Smolenskin founded 'Kadimah'; Herzl's friend ('der wackere Sohn Dr. Ruben Bierers Josef Bierer').

n_josef_roth.notes: Surgeon, long-time operator at the Czernowitz Jewish Hospital; trained Frankfurt/Berlin/Vienna; practice Str. Avram Iancu (Karolinengasse) 5. (A Lotti Singer thanked him 1935 - link ambiguous.)

n_josef_greif.notes: Banker (bank never named in the press); National-Zaranist; vice-president of the Jewish community ('the decisive factor', Ebner 1937); Kultusrat. Political partner Dr. Josef Hafner.

n_josef_hafner.notes: Advocate; chairman of the Vereinigung unabhängiger Juden executive (offered resignation 3.1930, refused). Co-led the Greif group.

n_max_rosenblum.notes: x Jetti Hochmann, civil marriage 13.11.1936 (he of str. Universității 7, she of str. Galiceanca 465). Press-real but every item a dead object. HYPOTHESIS (unproven): a Czernowitz relative of Fani's.

n_jetti_hochmann.notes: x Max Rosenblum 13.11.1936; of str. Galiceanca 465. Hochmann family context unknown.

n_getzel_axelrad.notes: Journeyman tailor (Schneidergeselle); x Rosa Rosenblum 25.11.1937, both of Str. Teținuhti 20. One press trace (the wedding notice). Azelrad = Axelrad spelling variant (Q890).

n_rosa_axelrad.notes: x Getzel Axelrad 25.11.1937 (both Teținuhti 20). Single-mention couple; no forward trace (Yad Vashem + marriage act are the routes). Whether she is one of Fani's sisters: UNPROVEN.

n_jakob_azelrad.notes: Elected Kultusrat 6.7.1937 (Liste 4). Azelrad (40 hits) = Axelrad (750 hits) spelling variant; kinship to Getzel unproven.

n_avram_axelrad.notes: b.1879 Bârlad, d.12.8.1963. Romanian-Jewish poet ('the poet of Jewish suffering'), publicist (pseud. A.A. Luca), publisher (Lumen 1908), translator; 'Ladita cu necazuri' (1919), republished 1945 as 'La raul Babilonului'. IDENTIFIED as the A. Axelrad of the Elias Hauster correspondence (Q1029/Q1047). No proven kinship to the Czernowitz Axelrads.

n_mechel_brender.notes: Großindustrieller of Czernowitz (textiles sector, 1934 'Fabrikant'); son Siegfried (Bucharest, engaged Paula Thau 1.7.1939); son Karl (stabbed Siegfried 1932). On the 31.3.1934 Verein committee with Schulim Brender. Kinship to Schulim/other Brenders unproven. The wealthiest Brender in the press.

n_siegfried_brender.notes: Son of Mechel Brender; of Bucharest; engaged Paula Thau (daughter of Jacob Thau, Storojineț) 1.7.1939. Sought by Rebeka Braun's 1972 notice. Postwar fate unproven.

n_karl_brender.notes: Son of Mechel Brender; stabbed his brother Siegfried 1932. No press trace after Nov 1932. (A different, older Karl Brender - Tricotania salesman - d.1937 Jassy.)

n_paula_thau.notes: Daughter of Jacob Thau (merchant, Storojineț); engaged Siegfried Brender 1.7.1939. Wedding unconfirmed.

n_dawid_brender.notes: Czernowitz furrier (Pelzhändler); d.19.1.1966 Nazareth-Ilit. Children: Rebeka x Konrad Braun, Tema Brender, Dr. Julius Brender (USSR). CORRECTION: Rebeka and Julius are DAWID's children, not Mechel's (Q1023/Q1025).

n_rebeka_braun.notes: Daughter of Dawid Brender; x Konrad Braun; of Nazareth-Ilit, alive 1972 (placed the 1.3.1972 search notice for brothers Dr. Julius and Siegfried). Children, husband's fate, burial not on the open web.

n_konrad_braun.notes: x Rebeka née Brender; of Nazareth-Ilit (1966).

n_tema_brender.notes: Daughter of Dawid Brender (1966 obituary). No other trace.

n_julius_brender.notes: Son of DAWID Brender (not Mechel - correction to R4 Q922). Of the USSR (1966); sought from Israel 1972. Field, emigration, later fate unknown.

n_simon_brender_cz.notes: Of Cernăuți; father of Dr. Zwi Brender; alive 1930 (Vienna promotion notice). Press-real 1924-1940 (8 hits), all sampled items dead objects. (Distinct from the two Radautz Simons already in the KB.)

n_zwi_brender.notes: Son of Simon Brender; Dr. jur. Vienna 17.7.1930; co-founder/chairman of Zeire-Zion Bukovina (1930s) until aliyah 1935; delegate Danzig 1932 + 18th Zionist Congress Prague; HOB Tel-Aviv leader 1960s-1980s. d.Feb 1982 (Die Stimme 1.4.1982 IN MEMORIAM, wife Chana).

n_leon_brender.notes: Sadagura merchant; vice-president of the Sadaguraer kaufmännischer Verein 1937 (= the 'Kaufmann Leo Brender' of the 27.2.1937 masked ball - Q1040). Father of Dr. Nathan Brender (Bologna 16.11.1939). 1938 marriage banns (salesman, Ion Creangă 47, x Paul Ledermann) may be him or a different Leon.

n_leo_brender.notes: Three press traces: 1926 Cludel wedding collector; 1931 silk-smuggling fence (convicted customs, acquitted in court); 1937 Sadagura merchant. Identity: one man or up to three - UNRESOLVED (Q916 NEGATIVE).

n_nathan_brender_cz.notes: Son of Leon Brender (Sadagura merchant); Dr. med. Bologna 16.11.1939 (after Italy's racial laws). Then vanishes from every accessible record. Possibly the 1926 Suceava 90-Lei donor as a boy (unproven).

n_schulim_brender.notes: Silk merchant: co-owner of Fa. Textua (1929 Ausgleich: 400k assets/1M liabilities); 1931 silk-smuggling co-principal (3.2M-Lei customs fine; acquitted 13.11.1931 with all 14 defendants); rehabilitated - arbitration court + Alte Chorschule synagogue board 1934; b.~1902, d.Apr 1971 Haifa (funeral 13.4.1971), Hitachduth Jotzej Haifa Aliyah/Klita committee. Obituary RECOVERED (Q1058).

n_hilda_brender.notes: Co-defendant in the 1931 smuggling trial (acquitted 13.11.1931). One press trace; kinship to Schulim unproven. (Also spelled 'Hilde Brendel'.)

n_lea_brender_cz.notes: Co-defendant in the 1931 smuggling trial (acquitted 13.11.1931). One press trace; kinship to Schulim unproven.

n_jakob_brender.notes: Merchant, b.~1889, of Piața Ghica Vodă 8. Co-owner (2/32) of the 1938 expropriated parcel with Abraham Wittner (1/2), Lotti Brender (1/4), Honora Ausländer (6/32) - probable husband of Lotti née Wittner (supersedes the Abraham-Brendar hypothesis).

n_lotti_wittner.notes: Co-owner (8/32) of the 1938 Piața Ghica Vodă parcel; address Piața Ghica Vodă. Birth family, marriage, children unproven; the Wittner family property (fasc. 3428 Cernăuți) is the archive route.

n_abraham_brender_suc.notes: Suceava Jewish donor (204 Lei, 7.3.1926, Beth-Hamidrasch 'd. Hopmeier Abraham Brender'); owned 1938-expropriated property on Piața Ghica Vodă, Czernowitz. (Distinct from the Radautz Abraham already in the KB.)

n_rosa_brender.notes: Engaged Bernhard Schäfler of Putila (17.3.1929) - the only press trace of either. Her Fleischer-married sister is unnamed.

n_bernhard_schaefler.notes: Of Putila; engaged Rosa Brender 17.3.1929. Single trace.

n_faul_ledermann.notes: Of str. Prutului 13; marriage banns with Leon Brender (salesman, Ion Creangă 47), 24.8.1938. No other trace.

n_israel_ungarleib.notes: Merchant. Fugitive chief suspect of the 1931 silk-smuggling affair (vanished 11.5.1931, arrested Bucharest ~15.5.1931); acquitted 13.11.1931. Resurfaced: x Sofie Herschmann, Sept 1936 (merchant, Str. Ion Creanga 31). Then press silence.

n_sofie_herschmann.notes: Of Piața Dacia 3; x Israel Ungarleib Sept 1936. One press trace (the marriage notice); age, family, fate unproven.

n_eusebie_hotinceanu.notes: Advocate of Czernowitz (first name FOUND 14.9.1938 AZ - Q1048): defended 13 of the 14 smuggling defendants (1931); Sparkasse directorate figure (resigned Nov 1931 amid scandal); stock-exchange president; 1931 defamation plaintiff. First name never in earlier press.

n_ernst_nastasi.notes: Attorney of Radautz; defended the absent Israel Ungarleib at the 13.11.1931 trial (acquittal rested on the statute of limitations); politically active (1939 voter list). No post-1939 trace.

n_bernhard_rosner.notes: Merchant (Testa); co-owner of Fa. Textua silk firm (1929 Ausgleich); 1929 chamber-of-commerce candidate. (Distinct from the Obermagistratsrat i.P. Bernhard Rosner d.1929.)

n_israel_schmidt_silk.notes: Merchant; co-owner of Fa. Textua (1929). Later traces ambiguous (name too common).

n_karl_kuemmel.notes: Merchant; co-owner of Fa. Textua (1929). No other Czernowitz trace.

n_israel_singer.notes: Convicted as fence (Hehler) in the 1931 silk affair; acquitted in court 13.11.1931. Zero press trace 1930-1940.

n_lotti_singer.notes: Convicted as fence 1931; acquitted 13.11.1931. Later traces ambiguous (1935 surgeon thank-you; 1939 Transylvanian marriage notice - both unproven).

n_eva_frischmann.notes: Co-defendant in the 1931 smuggling trial (acquitted). One trace.

n_jakob_jurgrau_ind.notes: Industrialist (described as 'frühere Industrielle' 1947). Communal career Czernowitz 1922-30 (Baukomitee Alter Chorschulverein 1922; Beth-Haroeh board; 1930 Bethaus/Spitals sections); office Karolinengasse 10; 1947 Radautz Mittelstandsküche committee. (Distinct from the many Radautz Jurgraus already in the KB.)

n_jacki_jurgrau.notes: Gura Humora - Transnistria - Kiriat Motzkin; d.6.6.2008, buried Afek-Zur Shalom, Kiriat Motzkin 8.6.2008. Widow Rachel (Uka); sons Michael Jurgrau, Israel Yogev; brother Shraga Yeshurun (historian). Co-founder of the Gura Humora landsmannschaft. Kinship to Bar's Jurgrau line unproven.
